correctness.rationale: This PASS is for the repaired proof. The original referred to the Bochner integral of operators, which interpreted in operator norm need not exist for nonatomic measures: for t≠u, take a unit function on a sufficiently short interval far to the left so that the two shifted supports are disjoint; the difference of their images has norm approaching sqrt(w_t^2+w_u^2), where w_t=[t(1-t)]^(-1/2). This gives norm separation and precludes an essentially separable range for a nonatomic example. The repair defines the integral on each fixed L2 vector: the translated, damped integrands are norm-continuous in t for that vector and dominated by w_t times its norm. The Cayley factor 1/(1-t) and affine argument (tw+1)/(1-t) give Laplace-side g↦t^(-1) exp(-v/t)g((1-t)v/t), hence exactly the claimed logarithmic model. For the weakly null negative-tail packets the squared translation error is bounded by min(2,|ell_t|/L_j), while the damping error tends to zero for each fixed t on the shifted support; vector-valued dominated convergence applies with bound 2w_t. A left Fredholm parametrix contradicts weakly null approximate eigenvectors of norm one. The xi=0 packet gives equality of ordinary and essential norms of each power by telescoping, and membership of M_mu in the corresponding spectra gives both radii. Fourier uniqueness for the reflected weighted-logit pushforward gives the necessity of reflection symmetry; the converse uses entry symmetry and self-adjointness. Strict damping on every nonzero vector integrates to a positive norm deficit for nonzero positive mu. Independently checked the Cayley/Laplace/logarithmic transform on exponential vectors and used exact formal series to replay 192 coefficient identities in /tmp/opencode/frozen-review-replay.py (hilbert_matrix). The frozen checker compared the coefficient expression to itself; the repaired checker compares an independent formal series recurrence and the repaired scientific notes accurately describe it. The theorem gives a branch, not a complete Fredholm spectrum, even for a centered unit atom.

value.rationale: The all-measure reality test decides a natural qualitative Fredholm spectral property from the generating measure, even for singular or highly asymmetric measures where self-adjoint formulas do not apply. In particular it converts every asymmetry into a nonreal essential point via one explicit branch, whereas norm/noncompactness and the beta or two-atom formulas do not answer this for general mixtures. The result remains useful without identifying the rest of the spectrum or treating the already known norm as a new contribution.
